_note: Fourth build: the first under chain 4.0.0 (candidate mode) and package contract 1.3.0. Five fixtures of three kinds: A/B/C are versions of one skill bundle, D a skill with no expectations, E a bundle with a bill of materials. D and E have no truth files yet (two independent reviews each, at promotion); their probe rows are ungraded, not guessed. artefact_dir is the candidates directory, which the loader does not read.
filled_by: coordinator, from the second build (pipeline/builds/artifact-consistency-sweep-v2: abandon, unconverged at review, 7/9/11 class findings on three rewrites) and its r2 open set
_gap_observed: llm-wiki-ingest build, 2026-09-02/03: review r0 15 findings (6 CLASS), r1 13 (6 CLASS), r2 11 (6 CLASS), each on a rewritten text; of r2's class findings, at least two ('stop' vs steps 6-7; 'no newer date') were present verbatim in the text r1 reviewed and r1 did not report them. The convergence rule stopped a fourth review; the shipped skill is marked unconverged-at-review. Cross-round check in the fixtures: 4 findings present in an earlier text and reported only later. Second build: the candidate lifted recall but no test cleared every check twice; the field trial named four gaps in the method (rule defined by heading, missing BOM, unpointed-file quote, step x instance-section) and a miscount (six counts, seven things); the arm prompt dictated an output shape and cost the ledger check.
candidate_sentence: Reviews a whole artefact for internal contradictions by enumerating every step-rule, step-step, step-check and description-body pair as a row and ruling on each, so that one review round reports every contradiction the text holds, and emits the findings list with quotes plus the step matrix of checkable and graded verdicts.
expected_failure: OBSERVED in the second build: the bare baseline (no dictated shape) reaches recall 0.64-1.00 but emits no ledger (0 of 6), no complete step matrix in 2 of 6, and exceeds the precision proxy in 2 of 6. The candidate's own text was red at class level in three successive reviews. The incumbent arm is the second build's final text.
trigger_terms: does the body contradict the rules
which step is graded by nothing
find every contradiction in one pass
threshold: Across k >= 2 repeats: zero regressions on correctness, no more than 20 percent worse on tokens or tool calls, and at least one win on correctness or shape that survives every repeat. A clean baseline does not stop the build; a win on shape alone satisfies the clause.

claims.claim: Three whole-artefact reviews of one artefact each reported a different set of class-level findings: 15/6, 13/6, 11/6 (findings/CLASS).
claims.locator: events with function review_artifact, phases 5.2 at 22:30:08, loop 1 and loop 2
claims.quote: RED with CLASS findings: (1) step 2 'no material ... s
claims.effect_size: 6 class findings per round on three rewrites
claims.limits: one artefact, one reviewer prompt, one model tier

claims.claim: A class-level contradiction reported in round 2 was present verbatim in the text round 1 reviewed and passed over.
claims.locator: findings[1] where 'SKILL.md step 2 (no material) vs steps 6 and 7', quote field
claims.quote: **no material** - no claim, no value, no newer date for any page: keep the raw, write the source-log row and the operation-log line, touch no page, stop.
claims.what_was_measured: presence of the quoted line in the round-1 text (git b7d546b) and absence of the finding in the round-1 review
claims.limits: the round-1 reviewer may have judged it instance-level and not reported it; the record has no such note

claims.claim: A checker that returns one row per examined pair lets 'found nothing' be told apart from 'did not examine'.
claims.quote: Make a checker return what it examined, so that "found nothing" can never be mistaken for "did not run".
claims.limits: a design rule for checkers; applied here to a review, which its author did not test

claims.claim: Anthropic's own guidance gives a grader two jobs: grade the outputs and critique the evals themselves.
claims.locator: section 'Who runs the test, and who writes the assertions'
claims.quote: You have two jobs: grade the outputs, and critique the evals themselves. A passing grade on a weak assertion is worse than useless — it creates false confidence.

You cannot see how it was written. Find every place where two parts of the artefact contradict each other or where a step cannot be checked or is graded by nothing.
